issues: 2.7 s wall, 8 packages, zero native/binary deps - the cheapest install imaginable

@jscad/modeling v2 is CommonJS: `import { primitives } from '@jscad/modeling'` throws at parse time under ESM; you must default-import and destructure. Cost one failed run before any modelling started.
No glTF/GLB serializer exists in the JSCAD org at all, so every item went out as STL and through the harness converter (export_path=stl-convert).

Colour is a modelling-level feature (colorize) that only survives to 3MF and OBJ. The OBJ writer emits `usemtl crimson` but writes no .mtl, so the colour names resolve to nothing; the 3MF is a real material file but trimesh cannot read 3MF in this venv (no lxml). STL drops colour entirely.

items.notes: TRUE rounded fillet, not a chamfer: roundedCuboid({roundRadius:0.10}) is a primitive, so the hardest part of the item is one argument. 21 pips subtracted as spheres r 0.22 centred 1.14 out (dent 0.08 deep, rim dia 0.34, 18 segments -> 0.06u facets on the rim). This item's booleans are fully manifold (0 open edges) because every cut lands on a flat face - contrast B2/B3/B5/B7, where cuts cross faceted curved surfaces. Colour: body and pips are separate solids (pip = a cap 0.001 smaller than the void it sits in, so the dent stays concave and reads dark), each converted with the harness --color and merged. Density knobs: BODY_SEG / PIP_SEG, both free to move up or down.

Body is ONE solid of revolution from a 7-point profile - skirt, 0.35 wall, bore and interior floor with no boolean at all; crenels are 8 pie-wedge subtracts, plus 3 blind slits and an arched door tunnel. Raycast-verified: slits bottom at r=1.48 leaving 0.23 of wall (they do not pierce), the doorway is open at z=1.0 and solid at z=2.6, merlons measure 0.56 arc at mid-wall, skirt 2.058 at z=0.1. 4 of the 7 attempts were a manifoldness bisection: subtract(cylinder, coaxial cylinder) is already non-watertight, and so is box-into-cylinder (12 open edges). JSCAD's BSP leaves T-junctions wherever a cut plane crosses a faceted curved surface; retessellate/snap/generalize do not fix it and the tool has no repair. 194 open edges = 8.2% of edges here. Density: SEG=64 gives 1504 tris against a 15k ceiling.

PARTIAL only against the spec's explicit 'watertight solid': the sweep itself is clean, the union with the column is not (174 open edges, 2.2%). extrudeHelical is a true native sweep - one 10-point U-profile, pitch 2.6, 2.25 turns, planar end caps for free, 3 lines of code. Gotcha worth flagging: it stands the profile up with rotateX(-90), so profile +y becomes -z and the channel sweeps upside-down and below the floor unless you mirror the profile first (nothing in the docs says so; the doc example is a symmetric circle, which hides it). Deliberate deviation: floor plate carried inboard to r=0.42 so the chute welds to the column - the spec's own numbers (floor 0.95..2.15 vs column r 0.5) leave a 0.45 gap. Verified by raycast: floor tops at 1.72 / 4.32 / 6.92 at bearing 0, i.e. pitch exactly 2.6, top end at 7.92 just under the 8.0 column.

JSCAD has no noise, no displacement, no subdivision - nothing native to reach for. Honest route: compute radius(theta, z) = taper + 5 root flares + 2-octave value noise in JS and hand extrudeFromSlices 58 rings x 112 points. Zero booleans, so zero hard edges, and the loft is fully manifold. Noise is sampled at the 3D surface position so it wraps with no seam at theta=0; measured fbm peaks +-0.8, scaled by 0.10 to land the relief at the spec's +-0.08, finest octave 0.22u against 0.06u vertex spacing. Second colour = a 0.014-thick shell generated by the same dish function, so bark and cut face mate exactly. Trap caught by measurement, not by eye: a 112-gon ring of radius 0.01 at the dish bottom earcut into one degenerate triangle, which the converter silently dropped and opened a hole - floor the ring at 7% of the rim. Also caught: the closed-loop shell came out inside-out (signed volume negative) and had to be geom3.invert-ed.

The grammar item, and JSCAD's best showing: one RULES table (out/rise/tilt/children/fan per generation), one recursive grow(), one bezier helper, and the whole 1-3-6 tree falls out in ~30 lines. hullChain of tapering spheres is exactly the right primitive for limbs - consecutive links share surface, so no open seams anywhere. What is NOT achievable: a true blend at a branch junction. Children overlap their parent, which joins without a gap but with a crease; JSCAD's only 3D rounding is expand() on a whole solid (verified: it offsets the entire body, not selected edges). 6 tips verified present, one connected component, 6707 tris at SPHERE_SEG=10 against a 20k ceiling. Bbox is not x/z symmetric because 3-fold symmetry never is; the symmetry axis is on the origin.

PARTIAL, and this is the item that exposes the tool. (1) JSCAD's text is a STROKE font: vectorChar returns polylines, so a glyph is not a solid until expand() gives the strokes width - outline fonts/TTF are not supported. (2) There is no bend, warp, deform or shrink-wrap, so an engraving CANNOT follow a curved face: a flat cutter across the 2.0-wide word would miss by 0.13 on a face that bows 0.217. Approximation shipped: each LETTER is cut as its own flat prism rotated about the cylinder axis to its own arc position, so every glyph is engraved on its local tangent plane; residual depth error inside one 0.45 glyph is w^2/8R = 0.006, a tenth of the cut. Verified by rasterising the finished face into a depth map (harness/probe raycast): it reads DICE cleanly, cut depth mean 0.048 / max 0.051 against a 0.05 target, border stands 0.060-0.063 proud. Body is 2D-section-and-extrude (manifold); the 74 open edges come from the frame subtract. Third gotcha: vectorChar's `height` is a font size, not cap height - glyphs come out 1.5x it, and at the naive setting the word was 3.05 wide and ran under the frame.

One subtract() call, 121 operands, no crash, no fallback, correct answer - robustness is real. Performance is the story: 54.8 s wall (repeatable: 54.82 / 55.59 on two passes) at sphere segments=24, versus 0.3-0.8 s for every other item in the battery. JSCAD folds subtractions sequentially into a growing BSP, so cost climbs with the accumulated result, not just the operand count. NO REPAIR APPLIED and none is available in-tool: 7636 open edges (9.0% of edges) are T-junctions, but winding is consistent and there are zero degenerate faces, so the mesh renders correctly and only fails a strict manifold test. Verified: all 120 sphere centres are now empty, 40/40 sampled clear points are still solid, 25/25 points inside the rotated reveal box are empty. Density knob is the sphere segments argument (also the main time lever).

iteration_loop.error_quality_notes: Two very different halves. Argument validation is genuinely good and specific - 'startRadius must be an array of X and Y values', 'The number of segments per rotation needs to be at least 3', 'numberOfSlices must be 2 or more' - typed at you before anything runs. Past that the tool is silent: it never reports non-manifold output, inverted solids, self-intersection or degenerate faces. All three of the expensive bugs in this battery produced a clean exit and a plausible file: a helix swept upside-down below the floor (undocumented rotateX(-90) inside extrudeHelical), a shell built inside-out (only visible as a negative signed volume), and one degenerate triangle that the STL->GLB step dropped, turning a watertight stump into a holed one. measurements.measureBoundingBox / measureVolume plus an external inspector are the only safety net, and the loop is fast enough (~2 s edit-to-GLB, 56 s for B7) that measuring after every change is cheap.

overall_notes: Determinism: every item was baked twice; all 7 STL sha256 hashes are identical across passes (no RNG in the library, and B4's noise is a seeded hash function). Density control: up AND down, everywhere - `segments` on every primitive, `segmentsPerRotation` on the helical sweep, my own ring/radial counts on the lofts. There is no tessellation tolerance (segments are counts, not error bounds) and no decimation, so density is chosen before the boolean, never after; nothing here was decimated. Every item came in well under its ceiling (5194/8k, 1504/15k, 5126/22k, 17916/30k, 6707/20k, 1992/14k) with room to raise segment counts several fold. Fillets: rounded PRIMITIVES exist (roundedCuboid, roundedCylinder, roundedRectangle) and 2D offset/expand takes corners:'round', which covered B1 exactly; what does not exist is a per-edge fillet on an arbitrary solid or a blend at a branch junction - expand() on a geom3 offsets the whole body (verified: a 2-cube becomes 2.2 with rounded corners), so B5's junctions are creases and B2's crenel edges are sharp. The single biggest structural finding: JSCAD's BSP booleans leave T-JUNCTIONS wherever a cutting plane crosses a faceted curved surface. Bisected in isolation - subtract(box, box) is manifold, subtract(cylinder, coaxial cylinder) is not (108 open edges), subtract(cylinder, small box) is not (12), extrudeLinear of a 2D annulus is (0). modifiers.snap / retessellate / generalize do not repair it. That is why 5 of 7 items report watertight=false while B1 (cuts into flat faces only) and B4 (pure loft, no booleans) are clean, and it is why the two structural workarounds worth knowing are: build bodies of revolution as ONE extrudeRotate profile, and build tubes as extrusions of 2D shapes with holes rather than as subtractions. For a three.js consumer this is cosmetically harmless (winding is consistent, normals are fine, no visible cracks at game distance), but any downstream step that needs manifold input - shelling, physics convex decomposition, 3D print prep - would need an external T-junction weld. Total battery: 37 minutes wall clock, 30 minutes of authoring across 7 items, 21 model runs.
